s: upright (standing tall, as of a soldier)
stramm.et: From Middle Low German stram. Cognate with Dutch stram (possibly also from Low German). Further origin uncertain.

s: aida cloth, meshed cotton or linen fabric used for cross stitch embroidery or carpet weaving
Stramin.et: Borrowed from Dutch stramien, from Middle Dutch stramijn, stamijn, from Old French estamin, estamine (“light wool”), borrowed from Latin stāmineus (“full of threads, fibrous”), from stāmen (“thread”).

s: to move one's legs (and arms) strenuously
The baby already kicks its legs.
Er warf sich auf den Boden und strampelte und brüllte.
He threw himself on the ground and kicked and screamed.
strampeln.et: 15th century, iterative of Middle Low German strampen. Related with stramm, Strumpf, and Dutch strompelen.
